diagnostic_evidence.quote: Showing that for all $j \in [r]$ there exists $k \in [r']$ such that $\bs{s}_{j,j} \mm \vec{\matW}_k^\CT \mm  \tU_{:,j} \neq \bs{0}$, hence $r' \geq r$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only shows that for each $j$ some generator $\vec{\matW}_k$ satisfies $\bs{s}_{j,j}\mm\vec{\matW}_k^\CT\mm\tU_{:,j}\neq\bs 0$; the map $j\mapsto k$ need not be injective, so the inference $r'\geq r$ is invalid, and under this minimum-cardinality reading of 'minimal' the statement is false. Counterexample: $n=2$, $\matM=I_2$, $m=p=2$, $\tX$ with tSVDM $\tU=\tV=\tI$ and singular tubes $\wh{\bs s}_1=(1,0)$, $\wh{\bs s}_2=(0,1)$ (t-rank 2). Then $\operatorname{Image}(T_{\tX})=\{((a,0),(0,b)):a,b\in\RR\}$ is generated by the single element $((1,0),(0,1))^\CT$, so $\{\bs s_{j,j}\mm\tU_{:,j}\}_{j=1}^2$ is not a minimal generating set. (The weaker claim that no proper subset generates is true and easily proved.)

failure_location.quote: The set $\{ \bs{s}_{j,j} \mm \tU_{:,j} \}_{j=1}^r$ is a minimal generating set for $\operatorname{Image}(T_{\tX})$ when considered as $\FFF_n$-module.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma as 'is a generating set, and no proper subset of it generates' (proved by multiplying $\bs{s}_{j,j}\mm\tU_{:,j}=\sum_k\bs z_{j,k}\mm\vec{\matW}_k$ by $\tU_{:,j}^\CT$ to force $\bs s_{j,j}=\bs 0$), or drop the minimality claim.
issues.overall_effect: Only this motivational lemma (used to motivate the t-rank definition) is unreliable in its minimality claim; the spanning part is correct and nothing downstream relies on minimality.
issues.title: Image-module lemma falsely claims a minimal generating set
issues.why_classification: A stated lemma is false under the reading its own proof argues for, so a substantive assertion must be withdrawn or re-proved; the repair is short and local with no downstream damage, which is more than minor but avoids major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, $\RR_n$ satisfies Eckart-Young optimality for tubal-length truncation (\Cref{def:optimality.prop}) if and only if, up to a permutation of its rows,  the matrix $\matM$ can be written as

Let $\RR_n$ be a real tubal-ring with length $\ell$ that satisfies Eckart-Young optimality for tubal-length truncation. Then, $\RR_n$ also satisfies Eckart-Young optimality for multi-rank truncations and t-rank truncations.

We remind that the motivation for defining the tubal-length of a tensor, and the consequent tubal-length truncation operation, is to assist in discovering necessary and sufficient conditions on $\matM$ for Eckart-Young type results to hold, \textbf{not with respect to our new, `madeup', definition, but with respect to the t-rank and multirank}.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose (echoed in the abstract, 'we provide a complete characterization of the family of tubal products that yield an Eckart-Young type result', and the conclusions) promises a necessary-and-sufficient characterization for the classical t-rank/multirank notions. What is proven is only: tubal-length EY (a notion introduced in this paper) iff $\matM=\matD\matQ$ (thm:necessary_sufficient_conditions_optimality), and tubal-length EY implies multirank and t-rank EY (thm:lengthopt_implies_multirankopt). The converse links needed for the claimed characterization — multirank EY implies tubal-length EY (required because the necessity lemmas lem:nec.opt.disjoint.idempotent and lem:nec.opt.intra.idempotent.ortho assume def:optimality.prop, i.e. tubal-length EY) and t-rank EY implies the $\matD\matQ$ structure — are never established anywhere in the source.

failure_location.quote: In what follows, we provide a complete characterization of those choices of transforms $\matM$ that yield Eckart-Young type optimality results for t-rank and multirank truncations of the tSVDM.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing converse arguments: (i) observe via lem:principal_length_and_multirank and lem:length_and_multirank_order_preserving that for a tubal-length $\bs\varLambda$ and its corresponding valid multirank $\bs r$ the truncations and feasible sets coincide, so multirank EY implies tubal-length EY, closing the characterization for multirank; (ii) prove necessity for t-rank EY (e.g. competitors at uniform multirank targets $(r,\dots,r)$ showing cross-ideal row non-orthogonality violates t-rank optimality); or restrict the prose claim accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's headline guarantee — that the family of tubal products yielding Eckart-Young type results is completely characterized — is delivered only for the newly introduced tubal-length criterion; the necessity direction for the classical t-rank (and, without an additional unstated lemma, multirank) notions is unsupported.
issues.title: Claimed complete characterization for t-rank and multirank optimality lacks the necessity direction
issues.why_classification: The gap is a missing necessity reduction: one part is an easy unstated lemma from the paper's own correspondence results, the other needs a new but contained argument; the characterized family is in fact correct for both notions, so a recognizable version of the claim survives without altering the main theorem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $\tX \in \RR_n^{m \xx p}$ as above, suppose that $\bs{p}_j \neq \bs{e}$ for some $j \in [q]$ where $\bs{e}$ is the multiplicative identity of $\RR_n$, then $\bs{t}_j = \bs{e} - \bs{p}_j$ is a nonzero element that is orthogonal to $\bs{p}_j$, i.e., $\bs{p}_j \mm \bs{t}_j = \bs{0}$.

failure_location.quote: which is a nontrivial linear combination of elements of $B$ that equals zero, therefore no generating set of $\operatorname{Image}(T_{\tX})$ can be a basis, showing that $\operatorname{Image}(T_{\tX})$ is not a free module.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis by one that actually forces non-freeness (e.g. t-rank one with $\bs p_1\neq\bs e$, or more generally unequal tubal-length components $\lambda_j$) and repair the nontriviality step accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Only this motivational example is affected; the surrounding narrative (the image is not always free, motivating module length) remains true, e.g. when the tubal-length components of $\tX$ are unequal, but the stated sufficient condition for non-freeness is false.
issues.title: Example falsely asserts the image module is not free whenever some singular idempotent is not the identity
issues.why_classification: A stated mathematical claim in a numbered example is false with an explicit counterexample, so its hypothesis must be changed and the argument redone; the fix is local and the subsequent development (module length, tubal-length) survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: establishing Eckart-Young optimality for multi-rank truncation.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof handles only multi-rank targets and ends at 'establishing Eckart-Young optimality for multi-rank truncation'; no argument is given anywhere for the asserted t-rank optimality. The missing step is routine (a t-rank-$r$ truncation is the multirank-$(r,\dots,r)$ truncation, and $\{\tY:\text{t-rank}\leq r\}$ equals $\{\tY:\text{multirank}\leq(r,\dots,r)\}$ since t-rank is the maximal slice rank), but as written the theorem claims strictly more than its proof establishes.

failure_location.quote: Then, $\RR_n$ also satisfies Eckart-Young optimality for multi-rank truncations and t-rank truncations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the few-line reduction of t-rank optimality at target $r$ to the just-proven multirank optimality at target $(r,\dots,r)$, using the identification of t-rank with the maximal transform-domain slice rank.
issues.overall_effect: The t-rank Eckart-Young guarantee that this theorem transmits to the paper's narrative (characterized transforms yield t-rank optimality) rests on an unproven clause of the theorem.
issues.title: t-rank optimality clause of thm:lengthopt_implies_multirankopt is asserted without proof
issues.why_classification: The completion is a short routine reduction from facts already in the paper; no claim, regime, quantifier or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then there exists a unique tubal-length $\bs{\varLambda} = (\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_\ell)$ under $\mm$ such that $\tX = \tX_{\{\bs{\varLambda}'\}}$ if and only if $\bs{\varLambda}' \geq \bs{\varLambda}$.
By \Cref{lem:length_and_multirank_order_preserving}, any tubal tensor $\tY$ such that $\lng_{\RR_n}(\tY) \leq \bs{\varLambda}$ is of multi-rank $\bs{r}'$ under $\mm$ satisfying $\bs{r}' \leq \bs{r}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Applied to $\tX_{\bs r}$, the lemma yields the tubal-length of $\tX_{\bs r}$, whose multirank is $\rho_k=\min(r_k,\rank(\wh{\tX}_{:,:,k}))$; when the target $\bs r$ exceeds the actual slice ranks in some components, $\lambda_j=\rho_{[\varsigma(j)]}<r_{[\varsigma(j)]}$, contradicting the claimed identity. With the smaller $\bs\varLambda$ the final deduction also uses the wrong inclusion: it establishes $\{\tY:\lng\leq\bs\varLambda\}\subseteq\{\text{multirank}\leq\bs r\}$, but concluding the inequality for all multirank-$\leq\bs r$ competitors requires the reverse inclusion, which fails for competitors with multirank between $\bs\rho$ and $\bs r$. The needed facts — $\tX_{\{\bs\varLambda\}}=\tX_{\bs r}$ and equality of the two feasible sets for $\lambda_j=r_{[\varsigma(j)]}$ — are true but do not follow from the cited application and must be argued directly.

failure_location.quote: We apply \Cref{lem:principal_length_and_multirank} to $\tX_{\bs{r}}$, and obtaind a tubal-length $\bs{\varLambda} = (\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_\ell)$ with $\lambda_j = r_{[\varsigma(j)]}$ for all $j \in [\ell]$ such that $\tX_{\bs{r}} = \tX_{\{\bs{\varLambda}\}}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\bs\varLambda$ directly by $\lambda_j=r_{[\varsigma(j)]}$, verify $\tX_{\{\bs\varLambda\}}=\tX_{\bs r}$ slice-wise, and invoke the order-preserving bijection to identify $\{\tY:\lng(\tY)\leq\bs\varLambda\}$ with $\{\tY:\text{multirank}\leq\bs r\}$.
issues.overall_effect: The multirank part of the proof of thm:lengthopt_implies_multirankopt is unreliable in the over-truncation regime (valid target multirank strictly exceeding the tensor's multirank in some component), although the theorem itself is true.
issues.title: Proof of thm:lengthopt_implies_multirankopt misapplies the length-multirank correspondence when the target exceeds the actual multirank
issues.why_classification: The assertion used is true and follows in a few lines from the paper's own correspondence lemmas; only the attribution to lem:principal_length_and_multirank and the direction of the inclusion need repair, with no mathematical loss.

issues.failure_explanation: The cross-term displays contain an index error: the coefficient of $\beta_j$ should involve $\overline{\alpha_h}g_{s,t'}$, not $\overline{\alpha_h}g_{s',t'}$ (and eq:lin1.aGb and eq:lin2.bGa are written identically although $\hbs b^\CT\matG\hbs a$ is the conjugate of $\hbs a^\CT\matG\hbs b$), so the derivative L in eq:lin.sum.derivative.b is wrong. Moreover, the conjugation chain derives $g_{t',s}=\overline{g_{s',t}}$ via an unjustified symmetry step ($\overline{[{\matMi_{:,t}}]^\CT{\matMi_{:,s'}}}=\overline{[{\matMi_{:,s'}}]^\CT{\matMi_{:,t}}}$, i.e. treating the Hermitian matrix $\matG$ as symmetric), while the subsequent deduction $g_{s',t}+g_{t',s}=2g_{s',t}$ requires $g_{t',s}=g_{s',t}$; the correct identities are $g_{t',s}=g_{s',t}$ and $g_{t',s'}=g_{s,t}$ (verifiable from the conjugate-column structure of $\matM^{-1}$), so the lemma's conclusion happens to be correct, but the proof's steps are false as written. The proof also implicitly assumes $d_j=d_h=2$ (using distinct $s,s'$ and $t,t'$) and never treats the cases $d_j=1$ or $d_h=1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the Wirtinger derivatives with the corrected indices, replace the conjugation chains by the correct identities $g_{t',s}=g_{s',t}$ and $g_{t',s'}=g_{s,t}$, and add the easier degenerate cases $d_j=1$ or $d_h=1$.
issues.overall_effect: The necessity of cross-ideal row orthogonality in the main characterization currently rests on a computation with false intermediate identities; repairing it requires redoing the algebra and the degenerate cases, not new ideas.
issues.title: Wirtinger computation in lem:nec.opt.disjoint.idempotent contains index and conjugation errors
issues.why_classification: The lemma's statement is true and every erroneous step is repairable by routine bookkeeping (no new lemma, construction or replacement architecture), so neither it nor the main theorem that uses it suffers any loss.
